minimum_head_selection_result.observation: min_accepted_generation=2 accepts both same-generation successors and therefore cannot uniquely identify the head. The missing information is branch choice, not freshness ordering.
minimum_head_selection_result.inference: Absent a protocol-fixed total-order rule operating over an independently trusted-complete candidate set, at least one independently trusted branch-selection fact is required. For this exact two-candidate fork, one bit is information-theoretically sufficient if candidate identities and their ordering are already fixed and complete; operationally, one independently trusted selected_head_digest is the minimal self-identifying content-bound datum because it both names and authenticates the chosen branch. The pair (min_accepted_generation=2, selected_head_digest=D2a) deterministically replays the fork decision without hosted coordination at replay time.
minimum_head_selection_result.policy_exception: A globally pre-trusted deterministic total-order policy can remove the need for a dynamic selected-head datum only if candidate-set completeness is independently guaranteed. Without that guarantee, an omitted competing branch can change the apparent winner, so the mechanism is not yet replay-safe under adversarial or incomplete packaging.
minimum_head_selection_result.package_completeness: pass only for the exact package that explicitly contains both D2a and D2b; completeness against omitted same-generation branches is unproven
minimum_head_selection_result.replayability: pass for the exact two-candidate package when an independently trusted selected_head_digest is supplied; min_generation alone fails unique replay
minimum_head_selection_result.hidden_executor_absence: pass for this exact symbolic slice: local deterministic classification plus repository state/evidence transport only
minimum_head_selection_result.quota_zero_assessment: The fork classification and head comparison require no hosted compute, runner, Codespaces, cloud storage, paid API/model, artifact service or finite credit. Repository transport is lightweight state/evidence transport; rate-limit handling remains cross-invocation rather than in-run waiting.
